artworks.title: The Fury Tisiphone at the Palace of Athamas
artworks.description: LACMA print: Tisiphone invades Athamas' palace — Ovid's named Fury bringing madness, serpents, and the blood-guilt that drives the king to kill.

artworks.title: Orestes Pursued by the Furies
artworks.description: Rahl's canvas: the Erinyes close on Orestes — Tisiphone among the pursuing sisters as nineteenth-century academic terror.

artworks.title: Orestes Pursued by the Furies
artworks.description: Sargent's late mural vision: torches and snaky hair drive Orestes — the Furies (Tisiphone among them) as modern American grand-manner nightmare.

artworks.title: Erinyes Drive Alcmaeon from the Corpse of Eriphyle
artworks.description: Fuseli's Zürich painting: the Erinyes hound a matricide from his mother's corpse — Romantic sublime for Tisiphone's sisterhood of blood-vengeance.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Supergiant's underworld roguelike features Tisiphone among the Fury sisters — Megaera's sibling as a boss of blood and broken speech.

popCulture.title: Aeneid
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Tisiphone guards Tartarus in Book VI — the Fury named at the gate of the damned.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book IV — Juno sends Tisiphone to drive Athamas mad: the Fury as agent of divine revenge.

popCulture.title: Tisiphone
popCulture.description: One of the three Erinyes — avenger of murder, Virgil's jailer of Tartarus, Ovid's bringer of Athamas' madness.
